title: TOPSTITCH STYLE PROPERTIES: Exaggerate Topstitch
content: ### Objective Express the caved line when topstitches are stitched on the real garment. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ Topstitch (Click Topstitch Style) ▶ Property Editor ▶ 3D ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guieline: Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ Topstitch (Click Topstitch Style) ▶ Property Editor ▶ 3D 2. Toggle on the 3D option. → 3D shadow is added under the Topstitch to express the caved line. 3. Use below options to adjust the caved line's Intensity or Thickness. Option | Description ---|--- Normal Map | Select the Normal Map. Intensity (%) | Adjust the caved line's intensity. Thickness | Adjust the caved line's thickness.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide to enhance topstitching on garments by adding a 3D effect to express caved lines through adjustable intensity and thickness settings.

title: Skive
content: ### Objective Add skiving effect on desired parts of a Pattern or all Patterns (ver2.3.0). ### Location Property Editor (Internal Shapes/Pattern Only) ▶ Bond/Skive ▶ Skive ### Operation 1. Select a pattern or an internal shape to express skiving with Edit Pattern or Transform Pattern tools. → Its properties appear in Property Editor. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor (Internal Shapes/Pattern Only) ▶ Bond/Skive ▶ Skive → The select Pattern/Internal Shape is now being displayed in a semi-transparent grey color. → A scrollbar appears, displaying the physical property of the pattern from the value range of zero ('0') to one hundred ('100') in Percentage (%). 3. Move the scrollbar to adjust as desired. 4. Activate the Simulate. → The area of the internal shape is now being displayed softer as if it has been shaved down.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for adding a skiving effect to patterns and internal shapes using the Property Editor in version 2.3.0.

title: Modify Piping Status
content: ### Objective Modify Piping status. ### Location 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move or Edit Piping ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move or Edit Piping 2. Right click on a desired piping to edit. → Piping pop-up menu appears. Pop-up Menu | Definition ---|--- Delete | Delete the selected Piping. Refresh All Piping | Re-drape all Piping. Deactivate/Activate | Deactivate/Activate selected Piping. Freeze/Unfreeze | Freeze/Unfreeze selected Piping. Quadranglate | Change Piping mesh to quads. Triangulate | Change Piping mesh to triangles. Hide | Hide selected Piping. Show All Piping | Show all Piping.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for modifying the status of piping in a 3D environment using the toolbar options.

title: Set Shortcuts (Above ver4.2.0)
content: ### Objective Change the default settings of the software menu according to user preference in User Settings. Upon restarting, the user settings of the software becomes the default settings. Shortcut keys, menus, graphic options, view controls, default files, font settings and other miscellaneous properties can be set in User Settings. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ User Settings ▶ Shortcuts Main Menu ▶ Settings/Preferences ▶ Preferences ▶ Shortcuts (ver 11) ### Operation 1. Navigate to the menu as below: Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ User Settings ▶ Shortcut Search (ver MD10) | Can search by menu name and shortcut key. When you select a search result, the location of the corresponding menu is displayed in the lower function window. ---|--- Function | Can search shortcuts based on the location of the menu. Click the menu for which you want to set a shortcut and press the desired key on the keyboard. Reset: Returns the hotkey to the program default settings. Delete: Deletes the set shortcut. ※Note: Click the reset button at the bottom of the dialog to return to the default setting.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on customizing software menu settings to user preferences, allowing users to set default shortcuts and properties that persist after restarting the software.

title: Desaturation
content: ### Objective Use this function to maintain the texture of texture images or patterns while changing colors. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Fabric ▶Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ Texture ▶ Desaturation ### Operation #### Shadow Intensity 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Fabric ▶Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ Texture ▶ Desaturation 2. Enter the Shadow Intensity value directly or move the scrollbar to adjust. → The Shadow Intensity is now being adjusted and applied. #### Shadow Brightness 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Fabric ▶Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ Texture ▶ Desaturation 2. Enter the Shadow Brightness value directly or move the scrollbar to adjust. → The Shadow Brightness is now being adjusted and applied.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on adjusting shadow intensity and brightness for texture images while preserving their original patterns and colors.

title: Offset Pattern Outline
content: ### Objective Extend or retract (ver MD10) the Pattern outline while maintaining its original shape. ### Location Right Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Offset Pattern Outline ### Operation 1. With the Transform Pattern tool or the Edit Pattern tool, select the entire or partial Pattern outline. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Offset Pattern Outline → The Offset Pattern Outline Window appears. 3. Adjust following options as needed. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- Direction | Extend | Extend Pattern Outlines. Retract | Retract Pattern Outlines. (ver MD10) ※Note: Only Distance can be modified when Retract is selected. Distance | Set how much in distance the Pattern outline is extended. Number of Offsets | Set the number of offsets to be created. Total Distance | Total Distance = Distance x Number of Offsets Create Internal Line | Create Internal Lines at where the original Pattern outlines existed. Side Segment Type | Perpendicular | Extends the Pattern outline perpendicular to the selected Pattern outline. Extend Side Segments | Extends the Pattern outline while matching the angles of the segments on either side. Mirror | Extends the Pattern outline based on the corner angle created with the selected Pattern outline and its adjacent one. Default Corner | Extends the Pattern outline all around the selected segment or Pattern. Right Angled Corner | Extends the Pattern outline all around the selected segment or Pattern and converting corners to right angles. Unfilled Corner | Extends the Pattern outline all around the selected segment or pattern, except for corners. 4. Click OK. → The Pattern outlines are offset according to the settings. → Curve points are optimized automatically. (ver MD10)
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide on how to extend or retract a Pattern outline while preserving its original shape using the Offset Pattern Outline feature.

title: Edit 3D Garment Measure
content: ### Objective Edit 3D Garment Measure. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Measurement ▶ Edit Garment Measure 3D Toolbar ▶ Edit Garment Measure ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Measurement ▶ Edit Garment Measure 3D Toolbar ▶ Edit Garment Measure 2. Click on a 3D Garment Measure to edit. → The selected 3D Garment Measure is now being highlighted. → Its properties are now being appeared in the Property Editor. 3. Modify the properties of 3D Garment Measure. Linear Garment Measure | Circumference Garment Measure ---|--- Name | Rename the Linear Garment Measure. | Name | Rename the Circumference Garment Measure. Length | Confirm the length of the Linear Garment Measure. | Surface Length | Confirm the length of the Circumference Garment Measure. Square Width | Modify the width of the square that appears at the end of the Linear Garment Measure. | Circle Diameter | Modify the circle diameter that appears with the Circumference Garment Measure.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for editing properties of 3D garment measurements to ensure accurate fitting and customization.

title: BUTTONHOLE STYLE PROPERTIES: Buttonhole Shape
content: ### Objective Change buttonhole shapes as desired. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Buttonhole Tab ▶ Property Editor ▶ Shape ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Buttonhole Tab ▶ Property Editor ▶ Shape 2. Click the drop down menu on the right. → Preset buttonhole shapes appear in the menu. 3. Select a desired buttonhole shape. → The buttonhole shape is now being replaced. → All other relevant buttonholes are also being replaced.
content_description: Easily modify buttonhole shapes by selecting from a variety of preset options in the Property Editor.

title: Reverse Arrangement Horizontally/Vertically
content: ### ### ### ### Objective Flip 3D Garment Patterns horizontally and vertically while maintaining its curvature. ※ Note: Flipping Patterns while maintaining its curvature is only applicable for patterns arranged with Arrangement Points. ### Location 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Pattern Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Reverse-Arrange ▶ Horizontally / Vertically ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Pattern Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Reverse-Arrange ▶ Horizontally / Vertically → The selected Pattern is now being flipped over horizontally/vertically while maintaining its curvature.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide on how to flip 3D garment patterns horizontally and vertically while preserving their curvature using the 3D Toolbar.

title: MODULAR MODE: Order of Use of the Modular Configurator Window
content: Follow the order of use of the Modualr Configurator window in order to construct and use an user data. To create a configuration file for the Modular Configurator, please follow the steps below: Open the Modular Configurator window ▶ Add an User folder by pressing (+) icon ▶ Press the Edit icon to switch to the Editor Mode ▶ If needed, add groups by pressing Add Group icon ▶ Designate the Modular file (.zmdr) to either be displayed or hidden for each group ▶ Designate the Modular file (.zblc) to either be displayed or hidden for each group ▶ Click Save button to save the structure file in the same folder as the Block ▶ Press Exit button when editing is done
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for using the Modular Configurator to create and manage user data and configuration files effectively.

title: Shrink Pattern
content: ### Objective Shrink or stretch 3D Garment Pattern horizontally and vertically without changing it in the 2D Pattern window. The default value is 100 percent (%) which indicates the natural state of the Garment material, in other words there is no artificial shrinkage or stretchiness. Use the function to express shrinkage after textile treatments such as garment washing, or use it temporarily to draw the inner layer against the avatar when dressing multiple layers of Garments for easier Simulation. ### Location Click Pattern ▶ Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ Shrinkage Weft/Warp ### Operation 1. Select a Pattern to shrink with 2D toolbar's Edit Pattern or Transform Pattern. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Click Pattern ▶ Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ Shrinkage Weft/Warp 3. Enter desired shrink values. → The Pattern in the 3D window is now being shrunk accordingly.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide on how to adjust the shrinkage or stretch of 3D garment patterns in a simulation environment, allowing for realistic garment fitting and layering.

title: Internal Rectangle Tool
content: ### Objective Create a rectangle inside a Pattern. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ Internal Rectangle 2D Toolbar ▶ Internal Rectangle ### Operation #### Create Internal Rectangle 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ Internal Rectangle 2D Toolbar ▶ Internal Rectangle 2. Click and drag within a Pattern to freehand an Internal Rectangle. 3. Release the mouse to complete the Internal Rectangle. ※ Note: While creating the Internal Shape, press down the Shift key on the keyboard to create a square (ver.5.1.0). While creating the Internal Shape, press down the Ctrl key on the keyboard to create it by the center point (ver.5.1.0). While creating the Internal Shape, press down the Shift + Ctrl keys to create a square Internal Shape by its center point (ver.5.1.0). #### Create Internal Rectangle with Measurement Input 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ Internal Rectangle 2D Toolbar ▶ Internal Rectangle 2. Click once within a Pattern. → The Create Rectangle window appears. 3. Enter appropriate values in the options indicated below. Width | Set width of an Internal Rectangle. ---|--- Height | Set height of an Internal Rectangle. Link width and height to adjust them in a fixed ratio. Position | Outline | Set left, right, top and bottom position of an internal rectangle on the basis of the outline of the Internal Rectangle (ver2.5.0). Center | Set left, right, top and bottom position of an internal rectangle on the basis of the center of the Internal Rectangle (ver2.5.0). ※ Note: Internal Shape Tool Group
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide to creating an internal rectangle within a pattern using both freehand and measurement input methods.

title: Bond
content: ### Objective Add bonding effect on desired parts of a Pattern or all Patterns (ver2.3.0). ### Location Property Editor (Internal Shapes/Pattern Only) ▶ Bond/Skive ▶ Bond ### Operation 1. Select a pattern or an internal shape to express bonding with Edit Pattern or Transform Pattern tools. → Its properties appear in the Property Editor. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor (Internal Shapes/Pattern Only) ▶ Bond/Skive ▶ Bond → The select Pattern/Internal Shape is now being displayed in a semi-transparent orange color. → By default, the same physical property as the selected Pattern/Internal Shape is now being added to the selected Pattern/Internal Shape. 3. Activate the Simulate. → The bonded area is now being displayed stiffer as if an interlining has been fused. 4. Repeat the first step again. → In the Property Editor, select a desired preset to change its physical property. → For more detailed adjustments, click on Detail. The lists on the drop-down menu are the same as Fabric's.
content_description: This web page provides a guide for adding bonding effects to selected patterns or internal shapes using the Property Editor in version 2.3.0.

title: Merge Vertex by Proximity at Export
content: ### Objective Merge vertices across patterns by proximity, without relying on sewing relationships, producing a single unified mesh which is "air-tight" across seams. This is especially useful for geometry which has been created using the Retopology Tools within Marvelous Designer. Once the new topology has been finalized, any sewing relationships are removed - so the previous sewing-relationship-based method of merging vertices at export would not be effective. * * * ### Location Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ OBJ ▶ **Merge Vertex By Proximity** **** ### Operation 1. Load a project file with either traditional dynamic Marvelous Designer (Delaunay Triangulation) pattern meshes or non-dynamic pattern meshes created with the Retopology Tools in Marvelous Designer. 2. Export the mesh through expanding the **File** dropdown-menu, selecting **Export** , then selecting **OBJ**. 3. Set the file path for the OBJ and click **Save.** **→** Export OBJ pop-up window appears. 4. Check the option box for **Merge Vertex by Proximity** , above the option box for "Unified UV Coordinates". **→** If the option is checked, the Weld and Thickness options are not available. 5. Set the **Merge Distance** in listed scene units (mm by default). 6. Preview the merged vertices in the (3D mesh) window.. **→** Vertices which will be Merged can be highlighted in Red. **→** Vertices which will not be Merged can be highlighted in Blue. 7. Click **OK**
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide a step-by-step guide for merging vertices by proximity in Marvelous Designer, enabling users to create an air-tight unified mesh suitable for exporting as an OBJ file.

title: Spiral
content: ### Objective Create a Spiral pattern in the 2D Pattern Window. * * * ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ **Spiral** 2D Pattern Window Toolbar ▶ Create Pattern Shape Dropdown Menu ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115000993027/________.png)**Spiral** **** ### Operation 1. Select the tool/menu indicated above under "Location". 2. Click in the 2D Pattern Window. → The Create Spiral pop-up Window appears. 3. After setting the options below, click OK. **Radius** | Set the radius at which a spiral pattern rotates. ---|--- **Length** | Set the length of the Inner/Outer segment of the spiral pattern. (the two values are linked - editing one will automatically adjust the other) **Side** | Set the Inside/Outside width of the spiral pattern's ends. (editing either will automatically adjust the Length values slightly) **Offset** | Adjust the spacing between spirals. The length you enter is the distance from the center of the spiral pattern to the center of the next spiral layer. **Direction** | Set the rotation direction (Clockwise/Counterclockwise) of the spiral pattern. → A spiral pattern is created.
content_description: Create intricate spiral patterns in the 2D Pattern Window with customizable options for radius, length, offset, and direction.

title: M:N Segment Sewing (2D)
content: ### Objective Easily sew multiple segments (M) to multiple segments (N) at once and edit them as a group. When the total length of multiple segments corresponding to M is different from the total length of multiple segments corresponding to N, N segments are divided in proportion to M segments. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ M:N Segment Sewing 2D Toolbar ▶ M:N Segment Sewing ※ Note: Hold down the Segment Sewing tool for a while to access the M:N Segment Sewing tool. ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ M:N Segment Sewing 2D Toolbar ▶ M:N Segment Sewing 2. Click on the segments belong to M segments. Then, hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete M sewing lines. → M sewing lines are highlighted in neon color. 3. As checking the Directional Notches, establish Sewing Lines on N segments. Then, hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete. → The Sewing Lines no longer appear in neon color. ※ Note: * While establishing M:N sewing lines, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the last action or hit the Esc key on the keyboard to cancel all actions. * When you click on an inappropriate segment while sewing, the segment appears in red and you cannot establish Sewing Line on the selected segment. * The length difference of the first and the second half of seams appears in blue next to the mouse cursor. When the difference is greater than 1 inch, it appears in red to alert the user.
content_description: The M:N Segment Sewing tool enables users to efficiently sew and edit multiple segments simultaneously, ensuring precise adjustments when segment lengths differ.

title: FABRIC PHYSICAL PROPERTIES: Adjust Internal Damping
content: ### Objective Use this function to set resistance against the bouncing speed of Garments. Increasing the Internal Damping value is going to cause the Garment to slow down as if it is in underwater, and lowering the value is going to cause it to bounce very quickly. ※ Note: Adjusting the measurement while putting Garments on does not make a noticeable difference. Therefore it is better to use during animation as it influences Garments when they are moving. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Fabric Property Editor ▶ Physical Property ▶ Detail ▶ Internal Damping
content_description: This web page provides guidance on adjusting the Internal Damping value to control the bouncing speed of Garments in animations.

title: BUTTON STYLE PROPERTIES: Button Material
content: ### Objective Change color and texture of buttons as desired. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Button Tab ▶ Property Editor ▶ Material ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Button Tab ▶ Property Editor ▶ Material 2. Adjust the texture, color, gloss , and opacity as desired.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for customizing the color and texture of buttons using the Property Editor in the Object Browser.

title: FABRIC PHYSICAL PROPERTIES: Adjust Buckling Ratio
content: ### Objective Use this function to reflect the tendency of Fabric trying to preserve its shape, and then being bent when applying certain amount of force. The closer the Buckling Ratio gets to 100 percent (%), the more it becomes easily bendable fabric such as silk and jersey. On the other hand, the closer ration gets to 0 percent (%), the more it becomes less bendable fabric such as denim and wool. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Fabric Property Editor ▶ Physical Property ▶ Preset ▶ Buckling Ratio ![Buclking.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438785781529)
content_description: Explore how the Buckling Ratio in the Fabric Property Editor helps you understand the bendability of various fabrics, from flexible materials like silk to stiffer options like denim.

title: [Mode] Modular (ver3.0.0)
content: ### Objective Customize your own design by simply combining and modifying Pattern Blocks. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Change the mode at the top-right corner ▶ Modular ### Operation 1\. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Change the mode at the top-right corner ▶ Modular → Block Editor window is now being appeared.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to empower users to effortlessly create personalized designs by customizing and combining Pattern Blocks in the Block Editor.

title: TOPSTITCH STYLE PROPERTIES: Topstitch Length
content: ### Objective Adjust the stitch length shown on the 3D Pattern. ### Location Topstitch Item Property Editor Length ### Operation Find and click the menu indicated in Location The length of the Topstitch will be adjusted according to the set values
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to guide users in adjusting the stitch length of the Topstitch in the 3D Pattern using the Item Property Editor.

title: FABRIC PHYSICAL PROPERTIES: Adjust Density/Weight (Ver. 2024.1)
content: ### Objective Use this function to express the weight ratio per unit (gsm). The higher the value, the heavier the fabric. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Fabric Property Editor ▶ Physical Property ▶ Preset ▶ Density/Weight (Ver. 2024.1) ![MD Video contents Quick Retrospective - Frame 5 \(1\).jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438836850969) ※ Note: * All versions before 2024.1 use "Density" in the Property Editor where Versions 2024.1 and after will use "Weight".
content_description: This web page provides guidance on using the Fabric Property Editor to determine the weight ratio per unit (gsm) of fabrics, with emphasis on the updated terminology introduced in version 2024.1.

title: 3D Segment Sewing (VER4.2.0)
content: ### Objective In the 3D window, easily establish Sewing Lines on segments of Patterns or Internal Shapes/Lines. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Segment Sewing 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ Segment Sewing ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Segment Sewing 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ Segment Sewing → All sew-able segments are bolded. → All Sewing Lines appear in both 2D and 3D windows. 2. Click once on the Pattern segment to establish the first half of the seam. 3. With the mouse cursor, hover over the segment to be sewn to the first half of the seam. Drag the mouse to make the the Directional Notches parallel to each other. Then, click to establish the second half of the seam. ※ Note * When Directional Notches are crossed, the Sewing Lines in the 3D window are crossed as well. When Patterns are simulated at this state, either one of the Patterns is reversed and then sewn to the other Pattern. * Use the shortcut to establish M:N Sewing Lines. For more detail, please reference M:N Segment Sewing. ※ Note: 3D Sewing Video
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide to establishing Sewing Lines on pattern segments or internal shapes in both 2D and 3D windows for efficient garment design.

title: Flattening as Straight Line
content: ### Objective Maintain a particular Line (Avatar) straight when flattening a Pattern. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Edit Line (Avatar) 3D Toolbar ▶ Edit Line (Avatar) ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Edit Line (Avatar) 3D Toolbar ▶ Edit Line (Avatar) → When the Avatar is draped, its Garment becomes translucent. 2. Right click on the Line (Avatar) to be flattened as a center front/back or a straight line. → The right-click pop-up menu appears. 3. Select Flattening as a Straight Line. → The selected line is bolded. → The selected line flattens straight.
content_description: This web page provides instructions to maintain a straight line on an avatar while flattening a garment pattern in a 3D design environment.

title: Copy/Duplicate Graphic Image
content: ### Objective Copy/paste or duplicate graphic images as needed. ### Location Right-click Graphics Pop-up Menu ▶ Copy (Ctrl + C), Paste (Ctrl + V) / Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern ### Operation #### Copy/Paste Graphic Image 1. Select a graphic image with Edit Texture tool or Transform Graphic tool in the 2D window. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right-click Graphics Pop-up Menu ▶ Copy (Ctrl + C), Paste (Ctrl + V) → The copied graphic image is now being followed on the mouse. 3. Place the copied graphic image at a desired location in the 2D window. #### Duplicate Graphic Image (ver2.3.0) 1. Select a graphic image with Edit Texture tool or Transform Graphic tool in the 2D window. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right-click Graphics Pop-up Menu ▶ Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern → The selected graphic image is now being duplicated to Symmetric Pattern. ※ Note: Duplicate Graphic Image can only be used on Symmetrical Patterns.
content_description: This webpage provides instructions for copying, pasting, and duplicating graphic images within the 2D window using the Graphics Pop-up Menu.

title: Select Mesh (Brush) (Above ver. 9)
content: ### Select Area ### Objective Use the select Mesh (Brush) tool to select the area you want ### ### Location Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment▶ Select Mesh (Brush) 3D Window Toolbar ▶ Select Mesh (Brush) ### Operation 1. Follow the path specified in Location. Set the desired intensity, size, and focal of the brush in the brush dialog. You can adjust the brush size using the [ ] shortcut on the keyboard. 2. Click on the desired part of the garment click and drag to select an area. When using the brush, you can see that the border is gradated according to the set intensity and focus. The area marked with dark green in the center is the area with 100% value, and the applied value gets smaller as it goes outward. The area becomes darker as you drag multiple times. 3. Press and hold hotkeys below to add/ delete the selection area. Shift Key: Toggle between the existing selection area. Shift+Ctrl key: The Selection area will be added unconditionally. Ctrl Key: The Selection area will be deleted unconditionally. 4. Right-click on the selection area ▶ Select Menu. The menu is also available in Select Mesh (Box) and Select Mesh (Lasso). ### Subdivision 1. Right click on selection area▶ Select "Subdivide" menu. Can use the "Subdivide menu" with Select Mesh (Box), Select Mesh (Lasso) as well. 2. The mesh of the selected area is divided twice. **Select** Generated subdivision area can be selected with the Select Mesh (Brush) tool and the Select/Move tool. **Delete** Press "Delete" Key after selecting subdivision to delete a subdivision area. **Property setting** Select a subdivision area to display the property setting window. 1\. Name: Set the name of selected subdivision area. 2\. Level: Subdivision level 1 (Default) divide mesh twice. Higher the level, the more the mesh divides into multiples. **Show/Hide** Show/Hide generated subdivision area by Main menu ▶ Display ▶ 3D garment ▶ Show Subdivision. ### [Partial Freeze ](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/4402355674649#h_01JWZ79XC1DRWP0SECKK72EVRV) 1. Right-click on the selection area ▶ Select Freeze Menu. The menu is also available in Select Mesh (Box) and Select Mesh (Lasso). 2. The mesh of the selected area is freezed. **Select** The created freeze area can be selected with the Select Mesh (Brush) tool and the Select/Move tool. **Delete** After selecting the freeze area, you can delete it by pressing the Delete key on your keyboard. **Freeze area right click select/delete menu** \- Delete Freeze Region: Delete the selected freeze area. \- Delete All Freeze: Delete all freeze areas. \- Select All Freeze: Select all freeze areas. **3D Pattern right click select/delete menu** Right-click on the 3D pattern to use the Partial Freeze menus. \- Select All Freeze: Select all freeze areas. \- Delete All Freeze: Delete all freeze areas. **Move** The created freeze area can be selected and moved with the Select / Move tool. ### [Partial Solidify (Above ver. 11)](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/4402355674649#h_01JWZ79XC2D0C3W2YKAH7CK2BR) 1. Right-click on the selection area ▶ Select Solidify Menu. The menu is also available in Mesh Select (Box) and Mesh Select (Lasso). 2. The mesh of the selected area is solidified. **Select** The created solidify area can be selected with the Select Mesh (Brush) tool and the Select/Move tool. **Delete** After selecting the solidify area, you can delete it by pressing the Delete key on your keyboard. **Solidify area right click select/delete menu** \- Delete Solidify Region: Delete the selected solidify area. \- Delete All Solidify: Delete all solidify areas. \- Select All Solidify: Select all solidify areas. **3D Pattern right click select/delete menu** Right-click on the 3D pattern to use the Partial Solidify menus. \- Select All Solidify: Select all solidify areas. \- Delete All Solidify: Delete all solidify areas.
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide on using the Select Mesh (Brush) tool to effectively select, modify, and manage areas of a 3D garment in a design application.

title: Sansar Export
content: ### Objective Export in the samd file format for use in Sansar. ### Location Main Menu File Export Sansar (Samd) ### Operation 1. Find and click the menu indicated in Location. The Save File window follows. 2. Enter the garment name into the ‘File name’ tab and press ‘Save’ to save the file. The file saves in the Sansar format.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for exporting files in the SAMD format for use in Sansar.

title: Move Button
content: ### Objective Move buttons as desired. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move Button ### Operation #### Move Buttons with Click-and-Drag 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move Button 2. Click and drag the buttons to the desired location on either of 2D or 3D Pattern. → The selected buttons are now being moved accordingly. #### Move Buttons with Distance Input (ver2.5.0) 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move Button 2. While click and dragging the buttons with left-click mouse button, click right-click mouse button in either of 2D or 3D window. → The Moving Distance window appears. 3. Enter desired value in the menu. Distance Moved | Sets the moved distance of the buttonhole from its original location. ---|--- Position | Sets the position of the center of the buttonhole from the left/right/top/bottom of the Pattern outline. 4. Click OK. → The buttonholes are now being moved according to the input value. ※ Note : * It is able to select and move multiple buttons at once in the 2D window (ver2.4.0). * The Gizmo for Select/Move Button tool has been changed from 2D rotation Gizmo to 3D translocation Gizmo (ver3.1.0).
content_description: This web page provides instructions for users to easily select and move buttons within 2D and 3D patterns using click-and-drag functionality or by inputting specific distance values.

title: Solidify
content: ### Objective Maintain desired draping state per pattern unit. For instance, solidify creases on the back of the knee area of a pair of jeans to maintain its shape while simulating (Ver 2.5.0). ### Location 3D Garment Right-click Pop-up Menu ▶ Solidify ### Operation 1. 3D Toolbar ▶Select a 3D Pattern with Select/Move tool. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Garment Right-click Pop-up Menu ▶ Solidify → The selected Pattern is now being solidified. 3. Follow the indicated guideline and adjust the Strength: Click Pattern ▶ Property Editor ▶ Bond/Skive ▶ Solidify ▶ Strength → The selected Pattern's 3D shape is now being solidified according to the Strength value. ※ Note: * 3D Statement * The higher the Strength value, the better the sustenance. * Right-click to open the 3D Background Options Menu ▶ Show/Hide Color [(Show/Hide 3D Color Ver. 2024.1)](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358311619225)[ ](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/32523191112473/preview/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJpZCI6MzI1MjMxOTExMTI0NzMsImV4cCI6MTcxNTk3NDk0Mn0.vTz8AEFpwglRHaNeFb09thKYnyuNna7SAvTfH7sSS8U)to hide the Solidify color display in the 3D window.
content_description: This webpage provides instructions for solidifying the draping state of 3D garment patterns to ensure shape retention, particularly in areas like the back of the knee for jeans.

title: ZIPPER: Assign Different Materials to Slider, Puller, Stopper & Teeth
content: ### Objective Allows for different materials to be assigned to different components of the zipper individually, giving the user more control over the look of their garment's fine details. ### Location 3D Window ▶ Zipper ▶ Property Editor ▶ Material ### Operation 1. Load garment. 2. Add Zipper with the Zipper Tool in the 3D Window Toolbar. 3. Select the Zipper Slider in the 3D Window. 4. Navigate to the Property Editor. → Under the 'Material' section, change the 'Type' to the desired material type. → Under Material ▶ Basic Parameters ▶ Texture, change the texture to the desired color or texture file. 5. Select the Zipper Puller in the 3D Window 6. Navigate to the Property Editor. → Under the 'Material' section, change the 'Type' to the desired material type. → Under Material ▶ Basic Parameters ▶ Texture, change the texture to the desired color or texture file. 7. Observe that the material on the Zipper Slider is different from the material on the Zipper Puller.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for customizing zipper components with different materials and textures, enhancing the detailed design of your garment.
